summary.intent: Land the weekly benchmark switch to the checker default (PR #442), address review findings (#238 snapshot leak), and make checker-default extract at least 2-3x faster than react-docgen-typescript while keeping Storybook fast.
summary.outcome: PR #442 was written up and merged into #441's branch, the snapshot-leak fix (10df5137) was confirmed on the guards branch, and a perf worker was started and restarted after a failure. The RDT-versus-checker speed numbers are not yet reported, and the worker had uncommitted changes at the end.

repo: The weekly, agent_eval.py and bench.py now run the default checker; UNIVERSE_VERSION was bumped to 5 in scripts/weekly.py so the first checker record is not compared against the structural wrong-rate baseline and does not open a false 'wrong types rose' issue.

BUDGETS in scripts/headline.py are {'ms': None, 'rss_mib': None} for all five corpora (mantine, chakra, shadcn, antd, spectrum) until measured in CI; a None budget opens no issue. Headroom rule in docs/measurement.md: after two scheduled runs, take the larger, set time to 1.5x and memory to 1.25x, rounded up to the next 0.5 s and 50 MiB.

Checker-path measurements (macOS arm64, release, --no-cache): gate-large (938 components) 5.8-6.35 s and about 970-990 MiB; Chakra-only (787) 5.2-5.4 s and about 760-780 MiB; 3x gate-large 14.7-15.2 s and about 1,050 MiB. The on-disk cache does not shorten the checker pass.

The Storybook addon already shows structural props immediately and waits up to semanticWaitMs (150 ms) for the checker. It also prefetches the first story at startup (prefetchStories=1). Missing: live upgrade of an open story when the checker finishes late, and prefetch beyond one story.
The 'budget' term has two meanings in the docs: the weekly resource ceiling on Caliper's extract cost, and the ADR 0026 latency budget of 150 ms for the first Storybook answer (cold measured 171 ms).
Docs record RDT at about 10.4 s per run with no incremental mode; the 17-39x faster-than-RDT claim applies only to --no-checker. There is no checker-versus-RDT figure yet.
Checker cost profile: about 37 µs per request and 141 ms for the 3,776 ChakraButton requests; the first-answer cost dominates, and the work runs single-threaded.

The #238 snapshot leak was fixed in 10df5137 on feat/in-process-guards: a refused createSnapshot/updateSnapshot now releases its snapshot via discard() in crates/semantic/src/checker.rs, with sibling fixes in on_demand.rs and rpc.rs.

code.finding: The refusal path for an over-nested file now calls discard(), releasing the snapshot created by the answer that was dropped; before, the ID was lost and the snapshot could never be released.
A snapshot made for a caller that stopped waiting is now released.

workflow: The classifier blocks `entire trail finding resolve` as an external write, so the agent could only report the finding as addressed and give the user the command to run.
A subagent hand-back message carries no user authority; the assistant verified the pushed SHA with git ls-remote before writing the PR body.
A subagent that dies mid-task can be restarted from its transcript and should be told to commit and push first, verifying the remote SHA, so work is not lost again.
Merge order for the stacked PRs is #440, then #441 (which carries #442), then slice 4, then the oracle run.

friction: The user's accidental /stop hit the speed worker, which then auto-restarted and later failed with an API ENOTFOUND error, leaving uncommitted changes in its worktree.
The Entire finding for #440 still shows open after the fix, and the assistant could not resolve it because the classifier blocked the write.
PR #442 showed an UNSTABLE merge state when the PR body was written, and the cause was not investigated.
The 6 s and about 1 GB checker cost made the earlier speed lead over RDT uncertain, and no same-corpus RDT comparison existed.
open_items: Speed worker on perf/checker-extract-speed must commit and push, prove byte-identical output against the current checker default (gate-large and Chakra-only), run construct:parity, determinism and the 600-edit memory gate, and re-measure RDT against Caliper over 3 runs.
Link the trail and write the PR body for the speed branch when it reports; do not merge it until the identity proof is back.
Storybook live-upgrade of an open story plus wider prefetch is waiting on the user's go and on #441 merging.
Merge #440 and #441, after which slice 4 can delete the process route, crates/tsc-client and the project typescript@beta fallback.
Run the single oracle pass and reword the speed headline to match the measured checker-versus-RDT ratio.
Record the corpus budgets after two scheduled weekly runs.
Resolve the Entire finding 01M778W5HQ7T once it is confirmed or the user allows it.
Close or ignore PR #434, which is already merged as an empty change.
